# Error Handling Checklist: SPEC-014B - Harness Adapter Manifest and Fake Registry

**Purpose**: Validate request-level and entry-level runtime-inventory failure requirements before task generation
**Created**: 2026-06-03
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Request-Level Error Precedence

- [x] CHK001 Is deterministic request-level error precedence specified for authentication, mixed scope, unauthorized resources, invalid filters, and server failures? [Resolved, Spec §FR-064]
- [x] CHK002 Are mixed invalid-input cases required to select the first applicable precedence class rather than returning nondeterministic errors? [Resolved, Quickstart §Runtime Inventory API Contract Verification]
- [x] CHK003 Are request-level errors required to happen before runtime inventory entries are derived? [Completeness, Spec §Error Handling Contract]

## Error Envelope Safety

- [x] CHK004 Is `runtime_inventory_error.v1` specified for request-level errors? [Completeness, Contract §Error Responses]
- [x] CHK005 Are request-level errors required to omit partial `entries` and raw user-supplied values beyond safe field names or closed codes? [Security, Spec §Error Handling Contract]
- [x] CHK006 Is bounded `500 runtime_inventory_unavailable` behavior specified without stack traces, SQL text, raw values, host paths, provider payloads, tokens, or secret-like values? [Resolved, Spec §FR-066]

## Entry-Level Fail-Closed Outcomes

- [x] CHK007 Are feature-flag-off, manifest invalid, unsupported capability/policy, timeout, governance, task, lifecycle, assignment, and sanitized-evidence failures defined as entry-level outcomes for authorized evaluations? [Resolved, Spec §FR-065]
- [x] CHK008 Are entry-level failures required to return deterministic reason codes and bounded evidence in `runtime_inventory.v1`? [Consistency, Spec §Fail-Closed Reason Codes]
- [x] CHK009 Is top-level authorization/filter failure behavior kept distinct from entry-level blocked-inventory behavior? [Clarity, Spec §Error Handling Contract]

## Unsupported Capability And Policy Errors

- [x] CHK010 Are unsupported capabilities required to fail closed with `capability_unsupported` rather than stalling or selecting fallback adapters? [Completeness, Spec §FR-037]
- [x] CHK011 Are unsupported approval, user-input, and timeout policy failures mapped to specific reason codes? [Completeness, Spec §Manifest Policy And Provider/Account Constraints]
- [x] CHK012 Are malformed policy declarations mapped to manifest validation failure rather than runtime ambiguity? [Clarity, Spec §Manifest Policy And Provider/Account Constraints]

## Manifest And Evidence Error Boundaries

- [x] CHK013 Are manifest validation failures bounded and separated from raw schema/validator exception output? [Security, Spec §Manifest Validation Failure Payload]
- [x] CHK014 Are sanitized evidence rejection failures required to omit unsafe evidence and expose only bounded rejection metadata? [Security, Spec §Sanitized Fake Evidence]
- [x] CHK015 Are over-cap diagnostics required to set truncation metadata rather than leaking extra values? [Coverage, Spec §Manifest Validation Failure Payload]

## Verification Quality

- [x] CHK016 Do success criteria require tests for request-level precedence and entry-level fail-closed outcomes? [Resolved, Spec §SC-015]
- [x] CHK017 Does the quickstart include precedence and bounded `500` verification? [Resolved, Quickstart §Runtime Inventory API Contract Verification]
- [x] CHK018 Are error-handling requirements measurable without invoking real harnesses, gateway calls, external processes, scheduler dispatch, or mutations? [Measurability, Spec §FR-051]
- [x] CHK019 Are UI error states required to stay bounded and avoid unsafe payload exposure? [Consistency, Spec §Agents Surface UX Contract]
- [x] CHK020 Are error classes traceable to closed reason codes or closed error codes where applicable? [Traceability, Spec §Fail-Closed Reason Codes, Contract §Error Responses]
